reading.body:
Box has positioned itself as infrastructure for enterprise AI by opening its content management platform to agent access through seven model context protocol (MCP) connectors that give AI systems read and write permissions across email, file storage, and physical mail services.

The connectors represent a strategy shift from Box as a storage vendor to Box as a middleware layer between AI agents and enterprise data. An agent with access to these MCPs can search documents in Dropbox, preview emails in live Gmail clients, inspect object storage, and send physical mail, all within a single workflow. This makes Box's platform a potential bottleneck for any AI system that needs to act on unstructured enterprise content. The company's $1.2 billion in annual revenue comes from its traditional content management business, but the AI surface area it is now exposing through these connectors positions it to capture value from agent workloads that require document understanding and action.

What this data does not show is how widely these MCPs are deployed, which models or agents use them, or whether enterprises are actually routing critical workflows through them. The connectors exist. Whether they become load-bearing infrastructure for AI scaling depends on adoption metrics not present here.

profile_text.body:
Box is a publicly traded company founded in 2005 and headquartered in Redwood City, CA, trading on the stock exchange under the ticker BOX. The company describes itself as providing an Intelligent Content Management platform that centralizes content storage, workflow automation, and collaboration for enterprise customers. Its platform is designed to handle unstructured data such as lease agreements, finance documents, sales presentations, and employee handbooks, with built-in security controls and compliance tools covering standards including GDPR, HIPAA, and FINRA.

Box AI is the company's primary AI product, positioned as an enterprise content AI layer that connects to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google to deliver real-time summaries, deep analysis, and recommendations across stored content. The platform also includes Box AI Studio for building and customizing AI agents, a drag-and-drop workflow builder for automating processes such as loan processing and employee onboarding, AI-driven security with deep learning-based malware detection, automated content classification, and an e-signature capability with unlimited free e-signatures. The company reports it received the highest possible scores in 13 criteria in an unnamed evaluation that designated it a Leader.

Box's most recently reported annual revenue, from its 10-K filing for the period ending January 31, 2026, was $1,177,253,000. The site holds 175 legal exposure records associated with California, though no specific cases are listed in the available data.
